subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What lifecycle contract should the active memory path support for review, edit, forget/tombstone, supersede, and conflict resolution?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the correct contract depends on durable storage, plugin API shape, privacy, rollback, operator UX, and migration choices that automation should not choose independently.

options.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle storage/provenance/status/API semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI PRs.

options.title: Land A Narrow Audit Slice
options.body: Use the draft Memory Audit work only as a partial review-queue path after its storage, safety, and proof blockers are fixed, while leaving edit/forget/conflict semantics tracked here.

options.title: Defer Broad Lifecycle Work
options.body: Continue current search/promotion/dreaming behavior and address concrete stale-memory symptoms in narrower issues until memory lifecycle becomes a higher priority.

recommendation.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle storage/provenance/status/API semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage and event-journal work is the strongest current-history signal for the lifecycle storage/provenance decision.
